tag: SpyTag003/ALFA tandem, P-flanked ALFA, GGGGS linkers
provenance: selected (Becca, 2026-10-18) to answer what a LOOP insertion costs in display relative to a free terminus. AVPR2 is the panel member that can: it is the strongest expressor (6,367 a.u. in Tedman, against a screen median of 873), so a loss is measurable against a high baseline, and it already carries a terminal arm (p0047) on the same receptor. ECL3 (293-306, 14 aa, v1) between TM6 (272-292) and TM7 (307-328); 9/4 residues of room, 5 from TM7, and no cysteine within 10 residues, so no disulfide is at risk. Terminal p0047 and this loop arm carry the SAME 51-aa cassette, so the pair varies position alone. That is what putting every arm on the full cassette bought: the earlier design paired a 51-aa terminus against a 19-aa loop and so varied position and cassette size together, which is why a third AVPR2 arm was drafted to collapse the confound. With the cassette held constant the confound is gone and that arm is unnecessary. CCR5 repeats the same position contrast on a weak expressor (302 a.u.; terminal p0042 against its S271 loop arm), so the two bracket the question at both ends of the range

tag: SpyTag003/ALFA tandem, P-flanked ALFA, GGGGS linkers
provenance: selected 2026-10-18 after the tag-sites session showed Q187 and 182 are both inside a confidently modelled HELIX (AF-P11836-F1-model_v6 residues 178-190 are a contiguous alpha-helical dihedral run at pLDDT 84-93, confirmed here independently of their pydssp), and 5.6 A from C167. Topology alone could not see that: 187 is outside the 167-183 disulfide SPAN yet 5.6 A from its cysteine in space. 146 is the best remaining CD20 junction -- a genuine 7-residue coil in the N-terminal half of the 142-188 run, RSA 0.73, 16.0 A clear of both cysteines, the largest clearance of any candidate measured. It fails ONE criterion, and softly: the tag-sites pipeline floors a DSSP loop at 8 residues and this is 7. Note that is a different gate from our MIN_LOOP_LEN, which measures the TOPOLOGICAL run (47 aa here) and passes it easily -- the two floors are not interchangeable

tag: SpyTag003/ALFA tandem, P-flanked ALFA, GGGGS linkers
provenance:
ECL3 (258-277, 20 aa, v1), moved off S271 on 2026-10-18 and then off F264 to the deterministic pipeline's own published site F263 (det_path surface_loop, residue_range F260-N268). S271 failed three ways on AF-P51681-F1-model_v6: pydssp calls it H in a helix contiguous from 269 into TM7 with no break, so the distal half of this loop is TM7's N-terminal extension; 5.6 A CA-CA from C269, under the 10 A floor; and buried at RSA 0.06. The earlier note called 271 safe for sitting two residues PAST C269 and outside the disulfide bracket, which is the Q187 error -- outside a span is not clearance. 263 is the one arm in this batch that needs no caveat: coil in a NINE-residue run 260-268, which clears the DSSP loop floor of 8 outright, RSA 0.70, 15.1 A CA-CA, pLDDT 91.6. It beats 264 on both exposure (0.70 against 0.39) and clearance (15.1 against 13.7). Same loop throughout, so the position contrast against the p0042 N-terminal arm is unchanged.

Clearances here are CA-CA, the convention features.py calibrates its 10 A floor on. CA-SG and nearest-heavy-atom are NOT a fixed offset from it and can fall either side: after-161 on MS4A1 is 11.3 A CA-CA but 10.0 CA-SG, while after-263 here is 15.1 CA-CA and 17.8 CA-SG. Mixing conventions at the boundary is a category error
